title: Rep. Michael Rulli Disclosed 5 Stock Trades: Sold Nvidia, Bought Microsoft
content:
Rep. Michael Rulli (OH-6) disclosed five stock transactions on November 18, 2026, dated October 28 to November 12: sales of Nvidia, Eli Lilly, Lumentum and Costco and one Microsoft purchase, each in the $1,001–$15,000 band.

Trade data: Bargo, compiled from U.S. House and Senate STOCK Act filings.

DateTickerCompanyType / sizePrice at trade vs. Nov 23 (Bargo est.)

Nov 4LLYEli Lilly and CompanySale, $1,001–$15,000$1,417.99 vs. $1,364.60 (−3.77%)
Nov 4MSFTMicrosoft CorporationPurchase, $1,001–$15,000$555.80 vs. $492.50 (−11.39%)
Nov 12COSTCostco Wholesale CorporationSale, $1,001–$15,000$1,092.21 vs. $1,097.91 (+0.52%)

Transaction dates: Oct 28, Nov 4 and Nov 12, 2026. Disclosure date: Nov 18, 2026 (6 to 21 days later). Member: Rep. Michael Rulli, OH-6 (House).

What's been disclosed

  • Four sales: Nvidia (NVDA) on October 28, Eli Lilly (LLY) and Lumentum (LITE) on November 4, and Costco (COST) on November 12, $1,001–$15,000 each.
  • One purchase: Microsoft (MSFT), $1,001–$15,000, on November 4.
  • Price since: Bargo's estimate puts Nvidia about 23.4% lower on November 23 than at the sale date and Lumentum about 13.1% lower, while Microsoft, which was bought, is about 11.4% lower.
  • Timing: the filing came 6 to 21 days after the trades, inside the 45-day window.

Quick FAQ

How long after the trades were they disclosed?
6 to 21 days after the trades, which were dated October 28 to November 12. The STOCK Act gives members 45 days from the transaction to disclose it.

Why are the amounts ranges?
Filings report value bands such as $15,001–$50,000 instead of exact dollar amounts.

Where does the price comparison come from?
It is Bargo's estimate, comparing the price on the transaction date with the November 23 price. It is not the member's actual execution price.
